extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, mathematics students, and readers interested in the aesthetics and evaluation of mathematical work
extracted.subtask_description: A canonical framework (G. H. Hardy) for judging the merit of mathematical work, centered on two master criteria — beauty and seriousness — with listed subcriteria, negative signs, and illustrative examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Aesthetic harmony of the pattern of ideas; the ideas must fit together in a harmonious way. "Beauty is the first test: there is no permanent place in the world for ugly mathematics."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat mathematics like art: look for harmonious arrangement of ideas, elegance of argument, and an overall sense that the result is aesthetically pleasing. Examples Hardy gives as touchstones are Euclid's proof of the infinitude of primes and the proof that sqrt(2) is irrational (short, surprising, deep, general). Anti-patterns: lengthy, messy computations or constructions that lack harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seriousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance, importance, depth — the work should have intellectual weight and lasting value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the work connects to fundamental ideas or opens substantial new directions; whether it addresses an important problem. Seriousness is manifested in significance of ideas, generality, and depth. Avoid valuing mere novelty or technicality divorced from meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generality (as a component of beauty)
rubrics_metrics.description: The idea is one of the constituents of many mathematical constructs; applies in many settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer results that are widely applicable rather than narrow, case-specific facts. General statements that subsume many special cases score higher on beauty. Cross-relation to seriousness: generality also increases significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth (as a component of beauty)
rubrics_metrics.description: The result depends on, and reveals, deep ideas; metaphorically 'geological strata' — the harder to prove, the deeper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the proof or concept penetrates to fundamentals and requires substantial conceptual insight. Depth often corresponds to nontrivial methods or links to foundational theory. Anti-pattern: results that are mere restatements of definitions or transparent consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexpectedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Surprise in the conclusion or the method; the result or technique is not obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value proofs or statements that contain a clever or unforeseen idea. Unexpectedness increases aesthetic pleasure and often indicates conceptual novelty. Anti-pattern: results that follow straightforwardly from routine manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inevitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Once seen, the result feels uniquely right; it seems the only natural conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A beautiful result should, in hindsight, seem inevitable — the argument fits so naturally that alternatives feel contrived. This is a subjective but powerful mark of elegance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimal hypotheses, minimal apparatus, no extraneous matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concise proofs using the least machinery necessary; avoid redundancy. Economy complements depth and generality: a short, sharp argument that achieves much with little is prized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of the underlying ideas (component of seriousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The work connects to other parts of mathematics and involves ideas of genuine mathematical interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the concepts introduced or used illuminate other fields, solve longstanding problems, or create useful conceptual tools. Anti-pattern: isolated computations without conceptual payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generality (component of seriousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The result applies in many settings (relisted under seriousness because generality contributes to significance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging seriousness, give credit to results whose scope reaches across contexts, implying lasting utility and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth (component of seriousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The result penetrates to fundamentals and is not superficial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seriousness requires depth: the work should reveal underlying structure or require substantial insight, not be a shallow observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ugliness / mere computation (negative criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics that is ugly or consists largely of routine computation counts negatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag results or expositions that are long, technical, and computational with little conceptual structure. Such work lacks the harmonious pattern that defines beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triviality (negative criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Results that are trivial or obvious from definitions are deficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Downweight claims that follow directly from definitions or routine manipulations; they lack depth, surprise, and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialness / isolation (negative criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Isolated curiosities with no broader connections are poor in Hardy's view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be skeptical of narrowly tailored results that do not interact with wider theory; they score low on both beauty and seriousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dullness (negative criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that offers no surprise or intellectual engagement is judged badly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid work that is uninteresting or predictable; lack of unexpectedness and lack of conceptual payoff make mathematics dull.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuing 'useless' pure mathematics over 'useful' applied mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Hardy's position: 'useful' applied mathematics is often trivial, whereas 'useless' pure mathematics tends to be the beautiful and serious kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an evaluative stance rather than a formal test: when assessing quality according to Hardy, prioritize intrinsic aesthetic and serious merits of pure mathematics over immediate practical utility. Note: historical counterexamples (e.g., parts of number theory) challenge this absolutist separation.
